cards.explanation: The answer is four. John 11:17 says Lazarus had already spent four days in the tomb when Jesus arrived. That's the number the text gives. I think this is a heavy part of the story, so I'll let that number sit.

The answer is False. Martha heard Jesus was coming and went out to meet Him, but Mary stayed at home. Only one sister goes out at that point. Mary gets there a little later, once Martha calls her aside.

The answer is that God will give Jesus whatever He asks. Martha says, “But even now I know that God will give You whatever You ask of Him.” Look at those two words after “But,” "even now." Her brother has been in the tomb four days, and she still says it to Jesus's face. I think that's some real nerve.

The answer is in the resurrection at the last day. Martha says, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.” She's got her answer ready, like someone who already knows the recipe. She's pointing to the last day, friends. Jesus is about to say something that changes how she hears it.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “Whoever believes in Me will live, even though he dies.” Even though he dies, friends. Jesus isn't skipping past death. He's saying what happens to the one who believes in Him.

The answer is that He is the Christ, the Son of God. Martha answers, “Yes, Lord,” and then says, “I believe that You are the Christ, the Son of God, who was to come into the world.” Notice she says it right after He asked, plain and sure. She doesn't have the whole story yet, but she knows who she's talking to.
The answer is quickly. John 11:29 says Mary “…got up quickly and went to Him.” She doesn't wait around. Martha says one sentence and Mary is already out of her seat.

The answer is to the tomb to mourn. The text says the Jews followed her, “…supposing she was going to the tomb to mourn there.” They were guessing, and as it turns out, the guess didn't match where she went. Mary went to Jesus.

The answer is True. Martha said, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.” Mary comes, falls at His feet, and says, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.” Same sentence, word for word. I think those words must have meant a lot to both of them.
The answer is “Where have you put him?” That's what Jesus asks, friends, and they answer, “Come and see, Lord…” That's all He asks in that moment.
The answer is “See how He loved him!” The Jews said it as they watched Jesus weep. That's what they saw. It's the first thing they say about it.

The answer is True. Some of them asked, “Could not this man who opened the eyes of the blind also have kept Lazarus from dying?” That's in John 11:37. The text says "…some of them…" and it comes right after others said, “See how He loved him!”
The answer is cave. John 11:38 says the tomb was a cave with a stone laid across the entrance. That stone is going to matter in a minute, friends. Keep your eye on it.

The answer is “By now he stinks.” And she doesn't dress it up. Martha, the sister of the dead man, says, “Lord, by now he stinks…” and then, “It has already been four days.” That's a woman who tells it straight.

The answer is that if she believed, she would see the glory of God. Jesus says, “Did I not tell you that if you believed, you would see the glory of God?” He's reminding her of something He already said. Then they take the stone away.

The answer is so the people will believe the Father sent Him. Jesus says, “…but I say this for the benefit of the people standing here, so they may believe that You sent Me.” He already knew the Father always hears Him. The prayer out loud was for the people standing there.
The answer is “Lazarus, come out!” Jesus called it out in a loud voice. It's three words, said loud, friends. And the man who had been dead came out.

The answer is False. Lazarus came out with his hands and feet bound in strips of linen, and his face wrapped in a cloth. He was still all wrapped up. Then Jesus tells the people there what to do next.
The answer is unwrap. Jesus told them, “Unwrap him and let him go…” Notice who He's talking to, friends: the people standing there. They get a job to do after the miracle.
